# Arūpāvacarakusala (Ds 2.1.3)

**ID:** Ds 2.1.3  
**Section:** Dhammasaṅgaṇī (ds)  
**Collection:** Abhidhamma  
**Title (Pali):** Arūpāvacarakusala  
**Title (English, from literature):** Good in Relation to the Universe of the Formless  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh01m.mul1.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh01m.mul1.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Arūpāvacarakusala* constitutes the section on immaterial or formless-sphere wholesome states within the *cittuppādakaṇḍa* of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, the first treatise of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Rhys Davids 1900; Gethin 2001]. Following the treatments of wholesome consciousness belonging to the sense sphere (*kāmāvacara*) and the fine-material sphere (*rūpāvacara*), it analyzes the wholesome dhammas pertaining to the formless realm (*arūpāvacara-kusala-citta*) [Rhys Davids 1900; Gethin 2001; Frauwallner 1995]. The exposition is structured around the four formless meditative attainments (*cattāri arūpajjhānāni*): the base of infinite space (*ākāsānañcāyatana*), the base of infinite consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatana*), the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*), and the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*) [Rhys Davids 1900; Bodhi 1999; Frauwallner 1995]. In classical Abhidhamma taxonomy, these four wholesome immaterial states constitute imperturbable kamma-formation (*āneñjābhisaṅkhāra*), functioning as the direct generative causes for rebirth in the four formless heavens (*arūpa-brahma*) [Van Gorkom 2009; Boriharnwanaket 2009].
